question.value: What are the molecular and dense gas inventory and ISM conditions of the strongly lensed z = 3.44 submillimetre galaxy SPT-S J002706-5007.4 using the new ALMA Band 2 receivers, and how will Band 2 perform for future high-redshift spectroscopic surveys?

claims.hypothesis: ALMA Band 2 receivers can simultaneously detect a wide suite of molecular and atomic transitions at z = 3.44, including transitions previously inaccessible to ALMA.
claims.experiment: Conducted an ALMA Band 2 Spectral Scan of SPT0027-50 from 76.87 to 111.03 GHz using twenty 1.875 GHz spectral windows and extracted line fluxes.
claims.result: Novel detections of CO(3-2) and HNC(4-3) at z = 3.44, along with CO(4-3), [C I](3P1-3P0), HCN(5-4), HCO+(5-4), and HNC(5-4), with fluxes within 1-sigma of archival Band 3 data.
claims.finding: ALMA Band 2 successfully provides a contiguous molecular and dense gas line survey of a high-redshift DSFG in a single spectral scan.

evidence.quote: I report the novel detections of the lines that were hitherto inaccessible at $z = 3.44$, CO($J$ = 3–2) and HNC($J$ = 4–3), as well as detections of previously-observed CO($J$ = 4–3) transitions, the neutral carbon line [C i]($^{3}P_{1}$–$^{3}P_{0}$), HCN($J$ = 5–4), HCO$^{+}$($J$ = 5–4), and HNC($J$ = 5–4), with fluxes in line with previous observations.

claims.hypothesis: The ISM of SPT0027-50 is characterized by highly excited, dense molecular gas exposed to an intense starburst radiation field.
claims.experiment: Measured CO(4-3)/CO(3-2), [C I]/CO(4-3), [C I]/L_IR, and HCN(5-4)/CO(4-3) ratios and compared them to thermalization limits, PDR models, and gas mass scaling relations.
claims.result: CO(4-3)/CO(3-2) flux ratio is 1.7 +/- 0.3 (near the 1.77 thermalized limit), [C I]/CO(4-3) is 0.30 +/- 0.06 implying n_H ~ 10^4.5 cm^-3 and FUV field ~ 10^3.8 Habing, and the dense gas fraction is 17 +/- 9 per cent.
claims.finding: SPT0027-50 contains highly excited, dense molecular gas in an intense starburst environment typical of DSFGs selected from wide-area surveys, with no evidence for significant AGN effects.

evidence.quote: The CO(3–2)/CO(4–3) flux ratio of $1.7 \pm 0.3$ approaches the thermalization limit, indicating highly excited, dense gas typical of vigorously star-forming systems at Cosmic Noon.
indicating highly excited, dense gas typical of vigorously star-forming systems at Cosmic Noon.

claims.hypothesis: SPT0027-50 has a clumpy internal dust morphology rather than a smooth, centrally concentrated distribution.
claims.experiment: Imaged high-resolution (50 x 44 mas) archival Band 7 continuum data and compared the flux in extended clumps between the four lensed images to the total emission.
claims.result: Star-forming clumps resolved on ~150 pc scales contribute 30-50 per cent of the total Band 7 continuum emission.
claims.finding: SPT0027-50 is a clear counterexample to the smooth-dust scenario, belonging to the class of gas-rich clumpy starburst systems at z ~ 3-4.

evidence.loc: A clumpy galaxy with Band 2 observations
evidence.quote: The clear clumpy morphology of SPT0027-50 therefore makes it a valuable counterexample to the smooth-dust scenario, and the gravitational lensing magnification, resolving structures on scales of order 150 pc, offers a rare opportunity to study individual clumps in a $z \sim 3.5$ starburst

High-resolution Band 7 continuum imaging reveals a clumpy lensed morphology in which star-forming clumps contribute 30–50 per cent of the total emission, resolving structures on scales of $\sim$150 pc.

claims.hypothesis: Incorporating ALMA Band 2, especially in the Wideband Sensitivity Upgrade (WSU) era, improves blind spectroscopic redshift search efficiency compared to Band 3 and Band 4 setups.
claims.experiment: Evaluated redshift identification probabilities and observing time ratios using the public optimisation tool from Bakx et al. (2022) across HerBS and SPT redshift distributions.
claims.result: Band 2 WSU configurations (8 and 14 GHz bandwidths) substantially increase the fraction of sources yielding >= 2 spectral lines, and Band 2 covers 50-100% larger redshift ranges per tuning than Band 4, becoming more time-efficient at z > 3.
claims.finding: Band 2 in the WSU era will substantially outperform the Band 3-only baseline and is the premier choice for blind redshift surveys at z > 3.

evidence.loc: Prospects of redshift surveys in the Band 2 and WSU era
evidence.quote: I find that Band 2 becomes significantly more efficient at $z > 3$, where the ability to cover a continuous frequency range without the “ladder”-like tuning overlaps currently required in Bands 3 and 4 outweighs the lower line fluxes.
Looking ahead to the WSU era, Band 2 configurations with 8 and 14 GHz instantaneous bandwidths substantially outperform the Band 3-only baseline for blind redshift searches

why_this_data.value: SPT0027-50 was selected as a Band 2 Science Verification target because it is one of the brightest z > 3 sources in the SPT sample and has bright spectral lines (including CO(3-2) and dense gas tracers HCN, HNC, HCO+) in the Band 2 frequency range.

evidence.quote: SPT0027-50 was selected as a verification target because it is one of the brightest $z > 3$ sources in the SPT sample. It has several bright spectral lines, including CO(3–2), at frequencies that before Band 2 were not available to ALMA

why_this_method.value: Used a singly-defined aperture based on the smoothed Band 2 continuum image widened by up to five beams to ensure extended flux is included and to allow direct comparison of line ratios.

evidence.quote: Using the average beam of the data cube, the aperture is widened by up to five beams if the signal-to-noise ratio permitted to ensure extended flux is also included in the flux measurement.
